drug_class: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB) combined with a Thiazide Diuretic
purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines two medicines in one pill to help lower your blood pressure more effectively than either medicine alone. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain.
how_it_works: The first part, olmesartan, works by blocking a chemical in your body called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to tighten. By blocking it, your blood vessels relax and widen, making it easier for your heart to pump blood. The second part, hydrochlorothiazide, is a gentle water pill that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and fluid from your body, which also lowers blood pressure.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, especially when standing up quickly. Increased urination (from the water pill). Low potassium levels which can cause muscle cramps or weakness. Headache, nausea, or upset stomach. Sensitivity to sunlight.
warnings: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Avoid if you have low potassium, kidney problems, or are allergic to sulfa drugs. Tell your doctor right away if you feel faint, have swelling of the face or throat, or notice signs of dehydration like extreme thirst or dark urine. Do not take with aliskiren if you have diabetes.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet (20mg/12.5mg) taken once a day by mouth. Your doctor may increase the dose over time if needed, up to a maximum of one tablet (40mg/25mg) once daily. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
